Records are written under `records/` (1,506 files, 3,782 KiB): `providers/<provider>.json`, `families/<provider>/<family>.json`, `contracts/<provider>/<family>@<revision>.json`, `reviews/<provider>/<family>.json`, and `sources/<host>/<id>.json`. `variants/` and `siblings/` are reserved and empty: the legacy repository holds no structured variant or benign-sibling data outside its fixtures (issue #4).

Every record carries an `externalRefs` entry with `system` `legacy-taxonomy-import` whose `id` is `<legacy sha>:<legacy path>` and whose `note` names the entry inside that file. That marker also identifies the files this tool owns; `--check` never touches other records.

## Every imported record is a draft

All imported records have `lifecycle: draft`. Import is not review: no record has passed the review-independence rule in `docs/governance/attribution.md`. The dossier verdict is preserved as a review-history event by the `legacy-import` automation actor, disclosed as `project-maintainer`. Promotion to `reviewed` is a separate, human step.

### Dossier verdict

| issuance-gated / T0 | 3 | researched | inconclusive | proposed |
| issuance-gated / T1 | 8 | researched | inconclusive | proposed |
| issuance-gated / T2 | 1 | researched | inconclusive | proposed |
| not-found / T0 | 1 | not-found | not-assertable | proposed |
| ready / T1 | 107 | researched | supports | current |
| ready / T2 | 44 | researched | supports | current |
| ready / T3 | 4 | researched | supports | current |
| rejected / none | 5 | rejected | does-not-support | proposed |

`currentContract` is set only for a `current` period. Gated, not-found, rejected and T0 families keep a `proposed` contract so their cited sources and open state stay resolvable without asserting a format.

### Evidence tier to evidence class

Tiers are read only as a description of evidence quality (ADR 0001). T1 is `provider-documented`, T2 `tool-corroborated`, T3 `project-policy`, T0 and no tier `unresolved`. No tier or class is a support status, and none is carried as one.

A stricter rule from `docs/governance/evidence-classes.md` is applied mechanically where it can be checked: a `tool-corroborated` claim needs artifacts from at least two distinct owners (Redact Secret's own repositories never count), otherwise the claim is imported as `unresolved`; a `provider-documented` claim needs at least one source.

| Downgrade | Claims |
| --- | --- |
| tool-corroborated with fewer than two distinct non-project owners, imported as unresolved | 104 |
| provider-documented without a source, imported as unresolved | 0 |

Lossy on purpose: `provider-example` and `provider-code` both become `provider-documented` because `evidence-classes.md` counts provider-published examples and official provider SDK code, but the legacy basis is kept in a `legacy-field-claim` external reference on the contract (`legacy evidence basis=...`). `community`, `maintainer-observation` and `research-hypothesis` are `unresolved`: none meets an evidence class without review. The legacy field status is a benchmark reliance flag (whether fixtures depend on the field) and is dropped, except that a legacy `unresolved` status forces class `unresolved`. Dropped statuses: frozen x489, provisional x78, unresolved x122.

## Ambiguous or lossy

| Item | Count | What happened |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contracts shared by several families | 8 | Legacy contracts are keyed by detector, and one detector covers several families. Claims and sources are attached to every family that shares the contract, each statement marked as shared; the shared regular expression is not attached to any of them |
| Families with no registry contract | 15 | Their contract holds only the dossier and taxonomy claims |
| Families whose contract tier differs from the dossier tier | 2 | The dossier decides the contract period; the registry tier decides only the claims it produced |
| Legacy links naming a tag or branch, not a commit | 139 | The schema forbids a live GitHub file locator, so the locator is the repository and the exact legacy URL is kept in a `legacy-url` reference. Resolving them to commit permalinks needs network access and is left to a follow-up |
| Source URLs with no known role | 124 | `sourceType` `other`: the legacy field that cited them does not say whether they are provider documentation, a scanner rule, or a write-up |
| Source URLs typed by review | 79 | Left as `other` by the mechanical import, then read and typed by a person while rewriting dossier prose into family narratives (issue #16, `scripts/migrate/authored/source-types.mjs`); only `other` is ever replaced |
| Claims with an inferred observed-at date | 339 | earliest date on the same contract (218), or the dossier researchedAt (4 contract claims, 117 taxonomy-source claims); legacy corroboration and reference entries carry no date |
| Field claims that look like historical variants | 14 | Not modelled as `variant` records: naming heuristics are not evidence. Listed for a reviewer: `azure-devops-personal-access-token:legacy-52-character-generation`, `datadog-application-key:legacy-40-hex-generation`, `elevenlabs-api-key:legacy-form`, `firecrawl-api-key:legacy-keys`, `fireworks-ai-api-key:unprefixed legacy key`, `gitlab-runner-authentication-token:legacy body`, `gitlab-runner-authentication-token:legacy partition segment`, `langsmith-api-key:legacy-ls__`, and 6 more |
| Statements or notes over 2000 characters | 3 | Truncated with an ellipsis; the full text is at the pinned legacy path |
| Provider not in the taxonomy provider list | 1 | `generic` is reserved by ADR 0002 for provider-less families; its dossier and six families exist in the legacy repository but no `providers[]` entry, so the record is derived |
| Detector mapped but no contract | 0 | none |
| Registry contracts with no family | 0 | none |
| Dossier evidence link not commit-pinned | 0 | none |

## Round trip

`tests/migrate-taxonomy.test.mjs` rebuilds the source set from the canonical records and checks it against the legacy URLs: all 932 distinct legacy URLs (with fragments) are recovered exactly from `locator`, the `legacy-url` reference and the citing `sourceRef.locator`.
